translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and ‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to us; they said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Humayd ibn Nafi‘, who heard Zaynab bint Abi Salamah narrating from Umm Salamah and Umm Habibah. They mentioned that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and said her daughter’s husband had died and her eye was troubling her, so she wanted to apply kohl. He said: “One of you used to throw a piece of dung after a year had passed. It is only four months and ten days.”

‘Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us—and the wording is ‘Amr’s—from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Humayd ibn Nafi‘, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, who said: When the death notice of Abu Sufyan reached Umm Habibah, on the third day she called for yellow perfume and rubbed it on her forearms and temples. She said, “I had no need of this. I heard the Prophet say: ‘It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for anyone for more than three days, except her husband, for whom she mourns for four months and ten days.’”
Zaynab narrated to him from her mother, and from Zaynab, the Prophet’s wife, or from a woman among some of the Prophet’s wives.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Nafi‘, who said: I heard Zaynab bint Umm Salamah narrating from her mother that a woman’s husband had died and they feared for her eye. They asked the Prophet’s permission to use kohl. He said: “One of you used to remain for a year in the worst part of her house, among its furnishings—or in the worst of its furnishings in her house. When a dog passed, she would throw a piece of dung, then leave. So why not four months and ten days?”

‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Nafi‘, with both reports: Umm Salamah’s report about kohl and the report of Umm Salamah and another of the Prophet’s wives, whom Zaynab did not name, like Muhammad ibn Ja‘far’s report.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, ‘Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. Yahya said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us; the others said: narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, from the Prophet, who said: “It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn a deceased person for more than three days, except her husband.”
Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz, meaning Ibn Muslim, narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Nafi, with the chain of al-Layth’s hadith and a report like his.

Abu Ghassan al-Mismai and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: I heard Yahya ibn Said say: I heard Nafi narrating from Safiyyah bint Abi Ubayd, who heard Hafsah bint Umar, the Prophet’s wife, narrating from the Prophet a report like that of al-Layth and Ibn Dinar. It adds that for her husband she mourns for four months and ten days.

Abu al-Rabi narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub; and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Ubayd Allah narrated to us. Both reported from Nafi, from Safiyyah bint Abi Ubayd, from one of the Prophet’s wives, from the Prophet, with the meaning of their report.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. They reported from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: A woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day may not mourn a deceased person for more than three days, except for her husband.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I recited to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, that Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi told him that ‘Uwaymir al-‘Ajlani came to ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi al-Ansari and asked, “If a man finds another with his wife, should he kill him, and would you kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah about it for me.” ‘Asim asked the Messenger, who disliked and criticized questions, and what he heard troubled him. When ‘Asim returned home, ‘Uwaymir asked what the Messenger had said. ‘Asim replied, “You have brought me nothing good; he disliked your question.” ‘Uwaymir said, “By Allah, I will not stop until I ask him.” He went to the Messenger among the people and asked the same question. The Messenger said: “It has been revealed concerning you and your wife, so go and bring her.” Sahl said: They mutually invoked curses while I was with the people. When they finished, ‘Uwaymir said, “If I keep her, I have lied about her.” He divorced her three times before the Messenger ordered him to do so. Ibn Shihab said: This became the practice concerning those who mutually invoke curses.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who told me that Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Ansari said that ‘Uwaymir al-Ansari of Banu al-‘Ajlan came to ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi. He related the report like Malik’s, adding that their separation became the practice. Sahl said she was pregnant and the child was attributed to its mother. The practice became that he would inherit from her and she from him what Allah prescribed for her.

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ibn Shihab informed me about the two who mutually invoked curses, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d’s report. A man from the Ansar asked the Prophet about finding another man with his wife, and the narrator mentioned the story. They invoked curses in the mosque, where he witnessed them. The man divorced her three times before being ordered to do so, and the Prophet said: “That is the separation between every two who mutually invoke curses.”

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his—‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, who said: During Mus‘ab’s rule I was asked whether the two who mutually invoke curses are separated. Not knowing what to say, I went to Ibn ‘Umar’s home in Makkah and asked permission. Though told Ibn ‘Umar was resting, he heard me and invited me in, saying only a need could have brought me at that hour. I found him reclining on a saddlecloth with a palm-fiber-stuffed pillow. I asked whether the two are separated. He said, “Glory be to Allah! Yes. The first to ask was so-and-so, son of so-and-so. He said, ‘If one of us finds his wife committing an indecent act, what should he do? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter; if silent, he remains silent over something similar.’ The Prophet kept silent. Later the man said it had happened to him. Allah revealed these verses in Surat al-Nur (24:6): ‘Those who accuse their wives…’ The Prophet recited them, admonished and reminded him, and said this world’s punishment is easier than the Hereafter’s. The man swore he had not lied. The Prophet summoned and admonished the woman, who swore he was lying. The man testified four times by Allah that he was truthful and a fifth time that Allah’s curse be upon him if he lied. The woman testified four times by Allah that he was a liar and a fifth time that Allah’s anger be upon her if he was truthful. Then he separated them.”

‘Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa‘di narrated it to me: ‘Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to us. I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr say: During Mus‘ab ibn al-Zubayr’s time I was asked whether those who mutually invoke curses are separated. I went to ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar and asked him. He mentioned a report like Ibn Numayr’s.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya’s. Yahya said Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us; the other two said he narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said the Messenger of Allah told the two who mutually invoke curses: “Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is lying, and you have no claim against her.” The man asked about his property. He said: “You have no claim to property. If you spoke truthfully, it was in return for what you were permitted of her; if you lied, it is even further from being yours.” Zuhayr’s narration says Sufyan narrated from ‘Amr, who heard Sa‘id say he heard Ibn ‘Umar report the Messenger’s words.

Abu al-Rabi‘ al-Zahrani narrated to me: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger separated the two brothers of Banu al-‘Ajlan and said: “Allah knows one of you is lying. Will either of you repent?”
Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, who heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr say: I asked Ibn ‘Umar about mutual imprecation, and he mentioned from the Prophet a report like it.

Abu Ghassan al-Misma‘i, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is al-Misma‘i’s and Ibn al-Muthanna’s. They said Mu‘adh, Ibn Hisham, narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from ‘Azrah, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, who said Mus‘ab did not separate the two who mutually invoked curses. Sa‘id said this was mentioned to ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said the Prophet separated the two brothers of Banu al-‘Ajlan.

Sa‘id ibn Mansur and Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Malik narrated to us. Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us and said: I asked Malik whether Nafi‘ narrated to him from Ibn ‘Umar that a man mutually invoked curses with his wife during the Messenger’s time, so the Messenger separated them and attributed the child to its mother. Malik said, “Yes.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us. They both said ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger conducted mutual imprecation between a man from the Ansar and his wife and separated them.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Sa‘id narrated it to us: Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, with this chain.

Zuhayr ibn Harb, ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr’s. Ishaq said Jarir informed us; the others said he narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abd Allah, who said: On Thursday night in the mosque, a man from the Ansar asked what would happen if a man found another with his wife: if he spoke, he would be flogged; if he killed him, he would be killed; if silent, he would remain angry. He swore he would ask the Messenger. The next day he asked the same. The Messenger said, “O Allah, open the way,” and supplicated. Then the verse of mutual imprecation (24:6) was revealed: “Those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves…” The man and his wife came and mutually invoked curses. He testified four times by Allah that he was truthful, then the fifth time invoked Allah’s curse upon himself if lying. The woman was about to invoke a curse, but the Messenger told her, “Wait!” She refused and invoked it. As they turned away, he said, “Perhaps she will give birth to a dark-skinned child with curly hair.” She did so.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: ‘Isa ibn Yunus informed us; and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us. Both reported from al-A‘mash with this chain, with a report like it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: I asked Anas ibn Malik, thinking he knew about it. He said Hilal ibn Umayyah accused his wife of being with Sharik ibn Sahma’, the maternal brother of al-Bara’ ibn Malik, and was the first man to mutually invoke curses in Islam. The Messenger said: “Observe her. If she gives birth to a fair-skinned child with straight hair and pale eyes, he is Hilal ibn Umayyah’s; if she gives birth to one with dark, kohl-like eyes, curly hair, and thin shins, he is Sharik ibn Sahma’s.” I was later told she gave birth to a child with the latter description.

Muhammad ibn Rumh ibn al-Muhajir and ‘Isa ibn Hammad, both Egyptians, narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Rumh’s. They said al-Layth informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Mutual imprecation was mentioned before the Messenger. ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi made a remark and left. A man of his people complained that he had found another man with his wife. ‘Asim said, “This has afflicted me because of what I said.” He took the man to the Messenger and described what he had found. The husband was yellowish, thin, and straight-haired; the accused man was stocky, dark-skinned, and heavyset. The Messenger said, “O Allah, make it clear.” She gave birth to a child resembling the man her husband said he had found with her. The Messenger conducted mutual imprecation between them. Someone asked Ibn ‘Abbas whether she was the woman about whom the Messenger said, “If I were to stone anyone without proof, I would stone this woman.” Ibn ‘Abbas said, “No. That was a woman who openly displayed wrongdoing in Islam.”

Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi narrated it to me: Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us: Sulayman, meaning Ibn Bilal, narrated to me, from Yahya, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The two who mutually invoke curses were mentioned before the Messenger, with a report like al-Layth’s. It adds after “heavyset”: “with very curly hair.”

‘Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us—and the wording is ‘Amr’s. They said Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said ‘Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: The two who mutually invoked curses were mentioned to Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn Shaddad asked whether they were the two about whom the Prophet said, “If I were to stone anyone without proof, I would stone her.” Ibn ‘Abbas said, “No. That was a woman who made her wrongdoing public.” Ibn Abi ‘Umar’s narration from al-Qasim says: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, meaning al-Darawardi, narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah al-Ansari asked, “O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him?” He said, “No.” Sa‘d said, “Indeed, by the One who honored you with the truth!” The Messenger said, “Listen to what your chief is saying.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ishaq ibn ‘Isa narrated to me: Malik narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah asked, “O Messenger of Allah, if I find a man with my wife, should I give him time until I bring four witnesses?” He said, “Yes.”
